newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian, Greek troops reach volatile Albania port.
newsitem.headline: Italian, Greek troops reach volatile Albania port.

text.p: Heavily armed Italian and Greek troops swept into the volatile southern Albanian port city of Vlore on Monday, securing a key bridgehead into the violence-racked nation in a coordinated show of force.

Nearly a week after soldiers from a multinational security force arrived in Albania and secured two other key ports of entry, Italian and Greek troops drove into Vlore early on Monday as Italian marines rushed ashore after arriving by sea.

In a spectacular landing, about 30 Italian tanks and armoured personnel carriers splashed onto the beaches near the port after landing craft brought them close to shore from a transport ship anchored about 1,000 metres outside the port.

Some 160 Italian marines leaped off their launches and hovercraft. With their rifles at a ready position, the soldiers immediately began searching buildings near the port, where the air was tense as sporadic gunfire rattled in the distance.
"Everything went well," said Italian General Girolamo Giglio after watching the well-orchestrated landing.
Vlore, which is 150 km (90 miles south of Tirana), and much of southern Albania have been controlled by rebel committees since an armed uprising that has claimed about 300 lives began in February.
The committees reject the authority of President Sali Berisha and demand his resignation. They blame Berisha for the collapse of get-rich-quick schemes that triggered the revolt.

The eight-nation U.N.-backed security force that will protect humanitarian aid convoys has been extraordinarily cautious about its plans for entering Vlore, where the violence began and the death toll has been high.

"Our first priority is getting the soldiers settled," General Giglio told Reuters Television. "The barracks are in poor shape and in need of repair. All the windows are broke. In about eight days we should be ready to deliver aid."

They are part of a 6,000-strong eight-nation force being led by Italy that began landing in Albania last Tuesday. The western port of Durres and Tirana airport were immediately secured last Tuesday by the forces.
More than 4,000 soldiers have arrived in Albania. France, Spain, Romania, Turkey, Austria and Denmark are also contributing troops.
General Giglio said he expected a total of 740 troops in Vlore on Monday. He said 450 Italian and 130 Greek soldiers were coming by land and another 160 Italians had arrived by sea.
The San Giusto transport ship that dropped anchor outside of Vlore port was accompanied by the cruiser Vittorio Veneto and a minesweeper Grecale. The San Giusto later steamed into the port.
Hundreds of Albanians watched from a distance as the sea landing unfolded. Many cheered and tried to shake the hands of the soldiers after they arrived and fanned out through the area.
"The people in the government couldn't handle the crisis alone so it is better that they come here to take care of the situation," said Viktor Gjata, a local resident.
Leaders of the Vlore town council held a rally in a central square to inform people about the landing.
Several thousand gathered to hear various local leaders urge them to support the soliders. One leader said Vlore would organise an official welcome ceremony on Tuesday.
"We should embrace the troops," one speaker said to a chorus of cheers. "They are our brothers."

General Giglio of the Italian forces also held a meeting with local authorities, including police chief Milto Kordha and the director of Vlore port, Hasko Hoxha, according to Medin Xhelili, the head of the local town council.
"He discussed how the troops will be deployed and that cooperation of the local authorities will be needed," Xhelili told reporters.
